groups.title: Community places and clubs

projects.title: Straddie Content Assets Kit

projects.title: Straddie Night Market Lab

groups.title: Co-operation, grants and contribution

projects.title: Straddie Tip Loop Lab

roleContext.title: What the office lets you do
roleContext.html:
The mayor chairs council, provides strategic direction to the CEO within the Act, appraises the CEO, participates in standing committees and speaks for council. Council makes collective policy and budget decisions; the CEO manages administration and staff. Mayoral directions cannot override a council resolution or adopted document, direct employee appointment or discipline, or require an unlawful act. Current Act, sections 12, 13, 104 and 170; Redland roles.

Point of overlapLever available through the role
Inside council responsibilitiesBuild support for policy, funded programmes, service improvements and council decisions.
State and federal responsibilitiesConvene, make submissions, seek funding, negotiate partnerships and advocate a council position.
Neighbouring councilsInvite joint learning, shared procurement or services where authorised, mentoring and coordinated funding proposals. Each council decides its involvement.
Businesses and community organisationsUnderstand needs, invite ideas, convene partners and establish fair routes to grants, leases or contracts within council powers.
Your projects and sole-trader businessChampion the public purpose while keeping any specific related-entity transaction subject to independent assessment and current interest/conflict rules.

A one-year programme is your planning choice. A by-election fills the existing electoral term; the next quadrennial election is in 2028. Election guide.

roleContext.title: Advancing your ideas without mixing the roles
roleContext.html:
Authorship of an idea does not by itself decide every conflict question. The assessment is about the actual matter, your interests and whether you may participate under the current law. Financial and non-financial interests both need attention. Disclosure alone does not authorise continued participation. Current Act; interests guidance.

Frame the public outcome first: lower household costs, useful skills, resilience or better access. Council can then consider transparent criteria, available approaches and delivery arrangements. If a particular decision could benefit you, Strange But True, your IP or equipment, or an organisation you later establish or join, obtain independent advice and apply the required process before taking part in that matter.

Keep personal and Strange But True finances, accounts and information distinct from council. General business conversations and public capability support should be separated from a live tender: Redland’s tender instructions direct tenderers away from councillor contact about the tender. Tender guidance. Any licence, donation, loan or access to your equipment needs clear terms and independent handling where interests arise.

For discussions with other governments and businesses, be clear whether you speak personally, for a future organisation if one is formed, or for council under an authorised position.

roleContext.title: The digital overlap
roleContext.html:
Your personal AI, community learning, Verse Box, C-hour, public simulation and resilience ideas can connect with council’s service and data responsibilities. Council’s public Digital Transformation Portfolio describes its existing systems work. It identifies existing systems, contracts and service responsibilities to connect with. Council programme.

For the 2027/2028 superintelligence scenario, the mayoral lever is to seek preparation across data, skills, service continuity, procurement, resident access and regional partnerships. The exact arrival date remains uncertain. Your Sovereign Capacity Lab provides a place to develop the scenarios. International investment intentions and realised spending should be distinguished when quoting figures.
